newsitem.title: CHINA: China employed up 1.5 pct at end-September yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China employed up 1.5 pct at end-September yr/yr.

text.p: China had 691 million people with jobs at the end of September, up 1.5 percent compared with the year-ago period, the Financial News said on Wednesday.
The number of employed in urban areas and townships reached 174.54 million, a rise of 2.9 percent from last year, the newspaper said.
The newspaper did not give the number of unemployed.
Officials have said the urban jobless rate is about 2.9 percent but has warned that this could rise as high as 7.0-8.0 percent by the end of the century.
More people had found jobs with private shops and businesses, with about five million more people finding work in that sector, the newspaper said.
China has been trying to reform its ailing state industries, pushing them to trim a bloated workforce and cut costs.
The average wage per worker paid in the first three-quarters of the year was 4,003 yuan, a rise of 14.2 percent from the year-ago period, the newspaper said.
Wages paid nationwide in January-September totalled 593.6 billion yuan ($71.5 billion), up 14.4 percent from the same period a year ago, it said.
Payrolls in state-owned enterprises were 458.75 billion yuan during the period, up 14.0 percent from the year before, it said but gave no further details.
